questions.question: Who was the President of Swaraj Party formed in the year 1923?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chittaranjan Das**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Swaraj Party was established on 1 January 1923 by Chittaranjan Das and Motilal Nehru.
 
• The two important leaders of the Party were CR Das and Motilal Nehru in which CR Das was the President and Motilal Nehru was its secretary.
 
• The Party was established as the Congress Khilafat Swaraj Party.
 
• The Swaraj Party sought greater self-government and political freedom from the British Raj for the Indian people.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In 1923, The Swaraj Party won the most seats during elections to the Bengal Legislative Council.
 
• Important leaders of the Swaraj Party included Huseyn Shaheed Suhrawardy, N C Kelkar, and Subhas Chandra Bose.
 
• In 1925, Swarajist Vithalbhai Patel became the speaker of the Central Legislative Assembly.
 
• This is the main achievement of the Party.

questions.question: The planned large-scale disruption of rail communications and the seizure of arms in Bengal were undertaken under the leadership of ________.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Jatin Mukherjee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jatin Mukherjee**, popularly known as **Bagha Jatin**, was one of the prominent leaders of the revolutionary movement against British colonial rule in India.
 
• He was known for his exceptional courage and leadership qualities, which earned him the nickname **"Bagha" (Tiger)**.
 
• The planned large-scale disruption of **rail communications** and the seizure of arms in Bengal were part of revolutionary activities aimed at overthrowing British rule.
 
• Bagha Jatin was associated with the **Jugantar Party**, a revolutionary group that operated during the early 20th century.
 
• He played a crucial role in mobilizing and organizing revolutionary activities in Bengal, including efforts to acquire arms and ammunition for the freedom struggle.
 
• Bagha Jatin was involved in the famous **German Plot**, which sought to secure weapons and financial support from Germany during World War I to fight against British colonial forces.
 
• His leadership and commitment to the cause of India's independence made him a revered figure in Indian history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Aurobindo Ghose**__

 __
 
• **Aurobindo Ghose** was a prominent leader of the Indian independence movement and later became a spiritual philosopher.
 
• He was initially involved in revolutionary activities but later shifted his focus to spirituality and established the **Aurobindo Ashram** in Pondicherry.
 
• He is known for his writings on **Integral Yoga** and his contribution to Indian philosophy.
 
 
 
• **Surendranath Banerjee**__
 __
 
• **Surendranath Banerjee** was a moderate leader in the Indian National Congress during the early phase of the freedom struggle.
 
• He emphasized constitutional methods and reforms to achieve independence and was one of the founders of the **Indian Association**.
 
• His approach was different from the revolutionary activities of Bagha Jatin and others.
 
 
 
• **Chittaranjan Das**__
 
 
• **Chittaranjan Das**, also known as **Deshbandhu**, was a prominent lawyer, freedom fighter, and leader of the Indian National Congress.
 
• He played a significant role in the **Non-Cooperation Movement** and advocated for Swaraj (self-rule).
 
• Though a key figure in the freedom struggle, his methods were more aligned with peaceful and non-violent means rather than revolutionary activities.

questions.question: Which of the following was a revolutionary organisation formed outside India in 1913?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Ghadar Party__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Ghadar party was an international political movement organized by Indians to end British rule in India.
 
 
• It was formed in 1913.
 
• Headquarters was at Yugantar Ashram in San Francisco, United States of America.
 
• It was founded by Sohan Singh Bhakna and Lala Hardayal.
 
• The Ghadar Party was organized by migrant Indians in the United States.
 
• The old name of the Ghadar Party was the Pacific coast Hindustan association.
 
• The name Ghadar party was adopted after the launch of its journal Ghadar in 1913.
 
• It was formally dissolved in 1948.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Bharatiya Janata Party was founded on April 6, 1980, and is headquartered in Delhi.

 
 
• It is based on the ideology of Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS).
 
 
 
• **Simon Commission: **
 
 
• The British government appointed the Simon Commission to review the Government of India Act 1919 in the year 1927.
 
• The Simon commission arrived in India in 1928.__
 
• It was formed to study constitutional reforms and make recommendations to the government in India.
 
• Simon commission was an all-white commission without any Indian members.
 
• The commission consisted of seven Englishman and sir John Simon was its chairman.
 
• It was formed on 26th November 1927.
 
• Simon commission arrived in India on __3rd February 1928.__
 
• The Madras session of the congress passed a resolution to boycott the Simon Commission.
 
• Simon commission submitted its reports on 27th May 1930.
 
 
 
• **Indian National Congress:**
 
 
• On December 28, 1885, the Indian National Congress was founded in Bombay by Scottish resident "Alan Octavian Hume".
 
• The first president of the Congress was "Vyomesh Chandra Banerjee".

questions.question: When was the All Bengal Students Conference held in the chairmanship of Jawaharlal Nehru?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1928**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The All Bengal Students Conference was held in 1928.
 
• Jawaharlal Nehru chaired the conference, marking a significant moment in the Indian student movement.
 
• The conference was pivotal in galvanizing student support for the Indian independence movement.
 
• It provided a platform for young intellectuals to discuss and address national issues.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru**

 
 
• He was a prominent leader in the Indian independence movement and the first Prime Minister of India.
 
• Nehru played a key role in shaping modern India with his vision of a secular and socialist nation.
 
• He was instrumental in establishing institutions of higher learning and research in India.
 
 
 
• **Indian Independence Movement**
 
 
• The movement aimed at ending British rule in India, culminating in independence in 1947.
 
• It involved a series of political and social campaigns, led by figures like Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, and Subhas Chandra Bose.
 
• Key events included the Non-Cooperation Movement, Civil Disobedience Movement, and the Quit India Movement.
 
 
 
• **Student Movements in India**
 
 
• Student movements have historically played a crucial role in Indian politics and social reform.
 
• They have been instrumental in advocating for educational reforms, social justice, and political change.
 
• Prominent student organizations include the All India Students Federation (AISF) and the National Students' Union of India (NSUI).
 
 
 
• **Bengal in the Independence Movement**
 
 
• Bengal was a major center for revolutionary activities against British rule.
 
• It produced several prominent leaders and revolutionaries, including Subhas Chandra Bose and Rabindranath Tagore.
 
• The region witnessed significant events such as the Partition of Bengal in 1905 and the Bengal Famine of 1943.

questions.question: Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith was founded by Shiv Prasad Gupta and Bhagwan Das in the year ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1921**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith was founded in the year **1921**.
 
• The institution was established by **Shiv Prasad Gupta** and **Bhagwan Das**.
 
• It is located in **Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh**.
 
• The university was initially known as **Kashi Vidyapith** and was later renamed to honor Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• The university was set up as a response to the Non-Cooperation Movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Non-Cooperation Movement**

 
 
• It was a significant phase of the Indian independence movement from British rule.
 
• It was led by Mahatma Gandhi after the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.
 
• The movement aimed to resist British occupation in India through nonviolent means.
 
 
 
• **Shiv Prasad Gupta**
 
 
• A prominent Indian philanthropist and freedom fighter.
 
• He played a crucial role in the establishment of various educational institutions in India.
 
 
 
• **Bhagwan Das**
 
 
• An Indian theosophist, scholar, and freedom fighter.
 
• He was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1955, India's highest civilian award.
 
 
 
• **Varanasi**
 
 
• Also known as Benares or Kashi, it is one of the oldest living cities in the world.
 
• It is a major cultural and religious hub in India, particularly for Hindus.

questions.question: On 8th April 1929, who among the following two revolutionists threw a bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly?

options.text: Bhagat Singh and Ram Prasad Bismil

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhagat Singh** and **Batukeshwar Dutt** threw a bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly on 8th April 1929.
 
• Their intention was to protest against the repressive laws being enacted by the British government.
 
• They did not intend to kill anyone; the bomb was thrown in an empty space to make a loud noise and attract attention.
 
• After throwing the bomb, both revolutionaries stayed at the scene, shouting slogans and distributing pamphlets.
 
• They were arrested on the spot and later faced trial for their actions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Revolutionary
 Description
 
 
 
 

 **Bhagat Singh**
 A prominent Indian revolutionary who played a key role in the Indian independence movement. He was known for his bravery and martyrdom at a young age.
 
 

 **Batukeshwar Dutt**
 An Indian revolutionary and freedom fighter who was associated with the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA). He is best known for his collaboration with Bhagat Singh in the Central Legislative Assembly bombing.
 
 

 **Central Legislative Assembly**
 The legislative body of British India where the bomb was thrown by Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt to protest against colonial rule.
 
 

 **HSRA**
 The Hindustan Socialist Republican Association, a revolutionary organization in India whose aim was to overthrow British rule through armed struggle.
 
 

 **Martyrdom**
 The death or suffering of a martyr. Bhagat Singh, along with other revolutionaries, became a martyr for the cause of India's independence.

questions.question: In the 1939 Tripuri Congress Presidential Election, Pattabhi Sitaramayya was defeated by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Subhas Chandra Bose**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the 1939 Tripuri Congress Presidential Election, **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** was defeated by **Subhas Chandra Bose**.
 
• The election was a significant event in the Indian National Congress as it highlighted the ideological differences within the party.
 
• Subhas Chandra Bose's victory was seen as a challenge to the more conservative and Gandhian faction of the Congress.
 
• Despite his victory, Bose faced considerable opposition within the party, leading to his resignation from the presidency later that year.
 
• This event marked a turning point in Bose's political career, eventually leading him to form the Forward Bloc and later the Indian National Army (INA).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subhas Chandra Bose** was a prominent freedom fighter and a charismatic leader who advocated for complete and immediate independence from British rule.
 
• He was known for his radical approach compared to the more moderate and non-violent approach advocated by Mahatma Gandhi and his followers.
 
• Bose's legacy includes his role in establishing the Indian National Army (INA) and his efforts to seek international support for India's independence.
 
• The 1939 election underscored the internal divisions within the Congress and the differing visions for India's path to independence.
